findings.title: Quick toggles start helper runs that can finish in either order, so the panel can end up in the opposite state from the switch.
findings.body: Each `PanelMsg::PanelRefresh` starts its own `pkexec aizome-panel-refresh on|off` thread, and nothing orders them. Example: turn the switch on, then off right away. If the `on` helper writes `/var/lib/aizome/panel-refresh` and the debugfs file after the `off` helper does, the panel and the saved choice end up on. The menu still shows off (`panel_refresh = Some(false)`), and a successful `PanelRefreshSet` never reconciles it. Both runs also write to the same temp file (`panel-refresh.new`) before renaming it, so one `rename` can fail with ENOENT, and that run reports a spurious failure. Fix: send helper calls through one queue, or skip new toggles while a run is in flight. After success, re-read `STATUS` (or clear `panel_refresh`) so the menu shows what the helper actually applied.

held.title: At boot, `apply` stops waiting if Intel's driver hasn't bound yet, so PSR stays at the kernel default (on) and the switch is hidden.
held.body: The wait loop stops as soon as `!helper::intel_display()` is true. The service is ordered only after `sys-kernel-debug.mount`, not after the GPU driver binds. If xe/i915 hasn't bound when the unit starts (for example, the module is still loading from udev coldplug or loading firmware), `intel_display()` returns false on the first pass. `run` then writes `available = false`, leaves PSR at the driver's default (enabled), and the menu shows no switch for the whole session. That breaks "off until turned on". Fix: wait the full timeout for a DRM device to appear (or order the unit after udev settles or the GPU device unit) instead of treating "no Intel driver yet" as "no Intel display".
